review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the definitions it relies on: orderedBox, boxKernel, OrderedBoxIndex, orderedBoxSimplexKernel, orderedBoxToSimplexKernel and its `_single` lemma, and mem_simplex. I grepped the library for `mem_orderedBox` and for simp calls that unfold orderedBox. I found no loops or competing rules; the file declares no simp attributes of its own. Both findings are missing simp lemmas, and they rest on repeated manual workarounds in the sources. I did not run Lean, so I have not tested the suggested lemma statements, and the downstream effect on existing `simp` calls is unchecked. The `orderedBox_inter_eq` orientation (∩ to a single box, used with `←`) looked acceptable and I did not report it.

findings.problem: `orderedBoxToSimplexKernel_single` is the canonical evaluation rule for the Finsupp.linearCombination-defined map on a basis element, but it is not tagged `@[simp]`. Its Mathlib counterpart `Finsupp.linearCombination_single` is `@[simp]`. Because the lemma is not simp, every use needs an explicit `simp only [orderedBoxToSimplexKernel_single, one_smul]`, here and in `BrownianIterated.lean` (`simpa only [orderedBoxToSimplexKernel_single, orderedBoxToRandom_single, one_smul]`). Plain `simp` would not normalise `orderedBoxToSimplexKernel n (Finsupp.single a c)`, because the map is a def that `simp` does not unfold.
findings.proposed_change: In BrownianIterated.lean, mark `orderedBoxToSimplexKernel_single` as `@[simp]`, and do the same for `orderedBoxToRandom_single`. The right-hand side `c • orderedBoxSimplexKernel a` is a smaller normal form and the lemma cannot loop. The call here can then become `simp` (or `simp only [orderedBoxToSimplexKernel_single, one_smul]` can be shortened).
findings.benefit: Plain `simp` can evaluate the formal-combination maps on single basis elements, as it does for `Finsupp.linearCombination`. The explicit lemma lists at the call sites can then go.

findings.declaration: orderedBox (missing membership simp lemma), used in orderedBox_emptyOrderedBoxIndex and exists_orderedBox_biInter
findings.problem: `orderedBox` is a plain def with no `mem_orderedBox` simp lemma, so the membership predicate `y ∈ orderedBox u v` is never normalised to `∀ i, u i < y i ∧ y i ≤ v i`. The file works around this by hand: `hy (0 : Fin (n+1)) (Set.mem_univ _)` followed by `change 0 < y 0 ∧ y 0 ≤ 0`, and the pattern `hy i (Set.mem_univ i)` at lines 108, 153, 157, 186 and 371. Other files unfold the def with ad hoc `simp only [orderedBox, Set.mem_pi, Set.mem_univ, Set.mem_Ioc, forall_const, ...]`. Each of these re-derives the same normal form without a shared simp rule.
findings.proposed_change: Next to the definition of `orderedBox` in WienerIntegral.lean, add `@[simp] theorem mem_orderedBox {n} {u v : Fin n → ℝ≥0} {y : Fin n → ℝ≥0} : y ∈ orderedBox u v ↔ ∀ i, u i < y i ∧ y i ≤ v i`. It could be proved by `simp [orderedBox]`, with `Iff.rfl`-style unfolding as a fallback. Then `hy 0`, `(hzb b hb i).1` and similar replace the `Set.mem_univ` and `change` boilerplate.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical, readable membership form. Proofs about boxes (empty box, intersections, density) can use `simp` or direct application `hy i`, with no `change` against the unfolded `Set.pi`/`Ioc` form, and later proofs avoid repeating the unfolding.
